policy_title: Introduce Laws for Independent Football Regulator
stated: The Conservative Party will introduce laws to ensure fans never face the threat of clubs joining breakaway competitions and to give them more voice through the Independent Football Regulator.

source.quote: We will introduce laws to ensure our fans never again face the threat of clubs in England joining breakaway closed-shop competitions and giving them more of a voice through the Independent Football Regulator.

bearing_set.reason: Football clubs are anchors of community identity and social trust in the UK; preserving the pyramid structure by blocking breakaway competitions and formalising fan voice directly bears on community belonging and civic participation indicators.

The Premier League is a major economic sector (>£8bn revenue, significant regional employment); regulatory constraints on club business models (blocking super-league revenue streams) and financial-sustainability requirements plausibly affect business investment, club viability, and local economic opportunity in a non-negligible way — with a genuine near-term/long-term tradeoff (constrained upside vs. reduced collapse risk).

membership_note: The policy's primary real-world effect is on community cohesion (O15) — football clubs as civic institutions — with a secondary but non-negligible bearing on prosperity (O13) through the economics of a heavily regulated major industry. Fan 'voice' mechanisms do not rise to O9's strict threshold (voting/democratic rights, anti-discrimination, due process); they are civic-participation features scored under O15.
